sources.title: AI Music Company Funding Tracker 2026: Valuations + ARR
sources.claim: Suno valuation $5.4B vs. Udio ~$200M+; total AI music funding $750M-$1B disclosed as of April 2026; Suno $300M ARR dwarfs Udio $3.1M ARR estimated

sources.title: Suno and Udio AI Music Lawsuit: 2026 Status and Timeline
sources.claim: RIAA v. Suno summary judgment hearing scheduled July 2026; Sony continues litigation against both Udio and Suno; UK text-and-data mining exemption revoked March 2026
data_points: $150K max per infringed work damages exposure

sources.title: Generative AI in Music, Film & TV 2026 — Market Forecast
sources.claim: 23% of newly released mobile games in 2026 incorporate AI-generated adaptive audio; gaming sector's real-time adaptive music demand is uniquely high-value vs. static soundtracks
data_points: adaptive game music under 100ms latency target
film/TV scoring via AIVA on 50,000+ productions
sources.note: Luminate report not directly accessible; figure cross-referenced with multiple secondary sources

notes: Market size figures differ by definition: 'AI in music' broad market ($5.55B, Research and Markets) vs. 'generative AI in music' narrow market ($229.5M, Grand View Research) — broad includes AI mastering, recommendation, and enterprise software; narrow covers only generative text-to-music tools
Udio ARR ($3.1M estimated) vs. Suno ($300M ARR) reflects very different business models and user acquisition — not necessarily Udio quality inferiority
UK text-and-data mining exemption revocation confirmed by multiple sources including TuneOnAI, Music Ally, and Chartlex AI lawsuits tracker

5Y growth (+550%) calculated from Research and Markets 2021 estimated market baseline (~$0.85B) vs. 2026 ($5.55B); narrow gen-AI music segment was essentially zero consumer revenue in 2021 (Suno/Udio launched 2023-2024)
